   Man arrested for stealing earbuds from shop in Changi Airport transit area

 CCTV footage showed a man taking the earbuds, valued at $347.71, at about 10.20am on Aug 2 and leaving without paying for them.
 PHOTO: ST FILE
 Marisa Yeo
 Published   Nov 16, 2026, 07:37 PM
 Updated   Nov 16, 2026, 09:18 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen SINGAPORE – A 38-year-old man has been arrested for allegedly stealing a box of earbuds at a shop in the transit area of Changi Airport Terminal 1.
 In a statement on Nov 16, the police said they were alerted to the case of shop theft on Aug 2 at about 12.30pm.
 A retail assistant discovered a missing box of earbuds from a display shelf while conducting a stock check, the police said.
 CCTV footage showed a man taking the earbuds, valued at $347.71, at about 10.20am on Aug 2 and leaving the shop without paying for them.
 The police were able to identify the man, who is a Hong Kong national, but he had already left Singapore.
 When he returned to transit through Changi Airport on Oct 29, officers from the Airport Police Division arrested him.
 The man will be charged with theft in dwelling on Nov 17. If found guilty, he may be jailed for up to seven years, fined, or both.
 According to the police’s mid-year crime statistics released on Aug 24, shop theft and theft in dwelling were among the top crimes of concern.
 Theft in dwelling cases increased slightly to 730 in the first half of 2026, compared with 726 in the first half of 2025.
